questions.prompt: You want to add a second provider to minidsh. With a model adapter in place, what do you change?
options: The agent loop, to branch on which provider is in use
The message assembler, to read the new provider's JSON
Nothing in the loop or assembler; you write a new class with a stream method
The event log, to store the new provider's raw stream
questions.explanation: Everything provider-specific lives inside the adapter's stream method. A new provider is a new adapter that returns the same chunks, so the loop and assembler stay as they are.

questions.prompt: What makes ScriptedAdapter useful for testing the agent loop?
options: It records real DeepSeek replies to a file
It fits the same interface, so the loop runs a whole turn on fixed chunks with no network
It checks that the loop sends valid JSON to DeepSeek
It makes model replies faster by skipping the assembler
questions.explanation: The loop only needs an object with a stream method returning chunks. A scripted one replays known replies, so tests are repeatable and need no API key.

questions.prompt: Where does a plug adapter stop being a good picture of a model adapter?
options: A model adapter translates between formats, so it must map meaning without losing or inventing any
A model adapter can only be used with one provider
A plug adapter has many methods, a model adapter only one
A model adapter changes the model's answer to fit your program
questions.explanation: A plug passes electricity through unchanged. A model adapter translates each provider's reply into the same chunks, which is why the chunk rules every adapter must keep are written down.
